content.title: About
content.content: No Fear Motherload is an energy drink containing caffeine, taurine, B‑vitamins and sugar. It is designed to boost energy, improve focus and speed up reaction time during intense physical or mental activities.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The drink is sold in 250 ml aluminum cans with a bold street‑racing inspired design.
Each can contains about 80 mg of caffeine, comparable to typical energy drinks.
The formula includes vitamins B3, B5, B6 and B12 to support metabolism.
No Fear Motherload is marketed as a "power charge" for athletes, gamers and active lifestyle enthusiasts.
The No Fear brand also offers energy bars and sports accessories.

items.title: Increased energy
items.content: Caffeine stimulates the central nervous system, temporarily raising alertness and reducing feelings of fatigue.

items.title: Improved concentration
items.content: Taurine and B‑vitamins help the brain work more efficiently, enhancing focus and reaction speed.

items.title: Metabolism support
items.content: Vitamins B3, B5 and B6 play a role in converting food into usable energy, potentially boosting metabolic rate.

items.title: Recovery aid
items.content: Sugar and electrolytes quickly replenish glucose stores and help maintain fluid balance after exertion.

items.title: Caffeine sensitivity
items.content: People sensitive to caffeine may experience nervousness, rapid heartbeat and sleep disturbances.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Excessive sugar can contribute to weight gain and increase the risk of dental cavities with frequent consumption.

items.title: Not for children or pregnant women
items.content: Due to its high caffeine and stimulant levels, the drink is not recommended for children, adolescents, pregnant or nursing women.

items.title: Medication interactions
items.content: Caffeine may amplify the effects of certain drugs, such as stimulants or some antidepressants.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Consume one 250 ml can 15–30 minutes before physical activity, training or mental work. Do not exceed 2–3 cans per day to avoid caffeine over‑dose.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the drink in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. Once opened, it is best consumed within 24 hours.

content.title: About
content.content: A light fruit smoothie is a refreshing drink made from fresh fruits, berries, a small amount of water or low‑fat yogurt, and no added sugar. It provides vitamins, minerals and antioxidants while remaining low in calories, making it an excellent choice for breakfast or a snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: A blend of berries and tropical fruits delivers a wide range of vitamins C and A.
Without added sugar, a serving typically contains no more than 120 kcal.
The fruit mix can be adapted to seasonal produce, making the drink environmentally sustainable.
Fruit smoothies are often used in sports nutrition for quick energy and electrolyte replenishment.
Blending retains most of the dietary fiber, contributing to a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and aids iron absorption.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Flavonoids and carotenoids from berries protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Low‑calorie
items.content: The modest calorie count makes the smoothie suitable for weight management.

items.title: Provides hydration
items.content: Water and natural fruit juice help maintain fluid balance.

items.title: Provides dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion and sustains satiety.

items.title: Fruit allergy
items.content: Some individuals may have allergic reactions to specific fruits used in the smoothie.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Although no sugar is added, natural fruit sugars can be a concern for people with diabetes.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Acidic fruits may exacerbate heartburn in sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Drink the smoothie immediately after blending to preserve freshness and nutrients. It can be added to a bowl of muesli, used as a base for protein shakes, or served as a light dessert.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the prepared smoothie in an airtight container in the refrigerator for no more than 24 hours. Shake well before drinking, as particles may settle at the bottom.

content.title: About
content.content: Gordita/sope is a thin corn shell used in Mexican cuisine to make the sope (a flat, round tortilla). This plain version is a ready‑to‑use product that can be quickly heated and filled with any desired ingredients.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditionally the sope dough is made from corn masa, water and salt, then cooked on a dry skillet.
The shell is crisp when dry but becomes soft and pliable after heating, allowing easy folding.
In Mexico, sopes are commonly topped with beans, meat, cheese and salsa, but the shell can also serve as a base for creative dishes like taco‑pizza.
The product has a long shelf life without added preservatives due to its low moisture content.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Corn shells contain virtually no fat, making them a lighter alternative to many grain‑based products.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Corn masa provides slow‑releasing energy, helping to maintain stable blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Gluten‑free
items.content: Made from pure corn flour, the shell is safe for people with celiac disease.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Corn fiber supports digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Corn provides thiamine, niacin and folate, which are important for metabolism.

items.title: Corn allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may be allergic to corn products and should avoid consumption.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some shell varieties contain added salt; people monitoring sodium intake should check the label.

items.title: Possible mycotoxin contamination
items.content: As with any grain product, improper storage can lead to mold and mycotoxin formation.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the shell on a dry skillet or in the microwave for 30–60 seconds, then fill with meat, beans, vegetables, cheese, guacamole or any topping you like. The shell also works for sweet versions with fruit, yogurt and honey.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place in an airtight package. For extended storage, keep refrigerated to prevent mold growth.

content.title: About
content.content: A vanilla ice cream bar is a frozen dessert shaped into a convenient single‑serve stick. It contains a dairy base, sugar, natural vanilla flavor, and stabilizers that give it a smooth, creamy texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The vanilla flavor is often derived from the seeds of the orchid Vanilla planifolia, though most mass‑produced bars use synthetic vanillin.
Bars are portable and melt quickly in the mouth, requiring no utensils.
The first commercial vanilla ice cream bar appeared in the United States in the 1970s.
In some markets the bars are coated with chocolate or nut crumbs for extra crunch and flavor.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: The dairy base provides calcium, essential for bone and tooth health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains riboflavin (B2) and cobalamin (B12), supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Small amount of protein
items.content: Milk protein contributes to tissue repair and satiety.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Bars contain a considerable amount of sugar, which can contribute to weight gain and increase the risk of dental caries.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: The dairy base may cause discomfort for people who are lactose intolerant.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to casein or whey may experience allergic reactions.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Keep the bar frozen and eat it straight from the wrapper. For a richer flavor, let it sit at room temperature for 1–2 minutes before consumption.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store at –18 °C or lower in an airtight package. Once removed from the wrapper, consume within 2–3 days to avoid sugar crystallization.

content.title: About
content.content: Pie NFS (code 2755) is a ready‑to‑eat dessert based on a traditional recipe with wheat flour dough, butter, and a fruit or berry filling. The product is manufactured according to food safety standards and sealed in an airtight film for extended shelf life.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pie NFS was first launched in 2021 as part of the “New Fruit Combinations” line.
The filling often includes seasonal berries such as raspberry, blueberry or cranberry.
The dough contains a small amount of vegetable oil, making it lighter than classic butter‑based pastries.
The product undergoes double thermal processing: baking followed by rapid pasteurization to increase shelf life.
The packaging is designed to keep the crust crunchy even after long storage.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: The pie provides carbohydrates that quickly supply the body with energy.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The dough contains vitamins B1, B2 and B6, supporting normal metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidants from berries
items.content: The berry filling is rich in anthocyanins, which help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Calcium and magnesium
items.content: Small amounts of calcium and magnesium are present, contributing to bone and nerve health.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Berries add dietary fiber, aiding normal digestion.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: The dough contains wheat flour, so the product is unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: The filling may contain added sugar, so individuals monitoring blood glucose should consume it in moderation.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Food preservatives may be used to extend shelf life, which can cause reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Temperature sensitivity
items.content: Storing at high temperatures can cause the crust to soften and lose its crunch.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pie NFS can be eaten straight from the package, warmed in the microwave for 30‑40 seconds, or served as a dessert with tea. For extra flair, add fresh berries or a light whipped topping.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, reseal the package tightly and consume within 3‑5 days. For longer storage, refrigeration is acceptable, though the crust may become less crisp.

content.title: About
content.content: Baked potato with the peel removed is a tuber that has been baked whole and then stripped of its skin. The flesh retains most of the nutrients, while the absence of the peel makes it softer and easier to eat.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Potato is one of the world’s most consumed foods, with annual production exceeding 350 million tonnes.
Baking preserves more vitamin C than prolonged boiling, where the vitamin is lost in the water.
The potato skin holds most of the fiber and polyphenols, so removing it reduces these beneficial compounds.
Baked potatoes are a staple in many cuisines: in Russia as a side dish, in the US as a classic “baked potato” with toppings.
There are over 4,000 potato varieties, differing in flesh colour, taste and starch content.

items.title: Rich in complex carbohydrates
items.content: Baked potato provides slow‑release energy, helping to maintain stable blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and aids iron absorption.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Potassium promotes normal heart function and helps regulate blood pressure.

items.title: Provides dietary fiber
items.content: Even without the skin, the flesh still contains a modest amount of fiber beneficial for digestion.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Baked potato is virtually fat‑free, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Solanine content
items.content: If a potato has sprouted or shows green spots, it may contain toxic solanine and should be discarded.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Baked potato has a high GI, so people with diabetes should monitor portion size.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Rarely, some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to potato.

items.title: Acrylamide formation
items.content: Prolonged high‑temperature baking can create acrylamide, a potential carcinogen; avoid over‑browning.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Baked potato without peel can be eaten plain, added to salads, soups, casseroles, or mashed. It pairs well with low‑fat cottage cheese, yogurt, herbs, and a drizzle of olive oil.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked baked potatoes in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Reheat in the oven or microwave to retain texture.

potato-boiled-from-fresh-peel-not-eaten-.title: Boiled Potato, fresh, peel not eaten, with oil

content.title: About
content.content: Boiled potato is a dish made from fresh potato tubers that are peeled, boiled until tender, and finished with a drizzle of vegetable oil. It has a soft texture, mild flavor, and a subtle buttery note.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Potato is one of the most widely consumed foods worldwide.
Boiling retains most of the vitamin C that is lost during frying.
Removing the peel makes boiled potato easier to digest, especially for people with gastrointestinal sensitivities.
A small amount of oil enhances flavor and improves absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins.
There are over 4,000 potato varieties, but high‑starch types are preferred for boiling.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Boiled potato retains a good amount of vitamin C, which supports immune function and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate blood pressure and supports muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Even without the skin, the flesh provides modest fiber that aids digestion.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Plain boiled potato is virtually fat‑free; a drizzle of oil adds healthy fats for a balanced meal.

items.title: Complex carbohydrates
items.content: The starch in potatoes provides a steady source of energy.

items.title: Potato allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may experience allergic reactions to potato.

items.title: Solanine content
items.content: Improper storage (greening) can lead to solanine formation, a toxic compound that should be avoided.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Boiled potato has a high glycemic index, which can cause rapid blood‑sugar spikes.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve boiled potato as a side dish, in salads, mashed, or cubed with oil, salt, and herbs. It can be added to soups or used as a base for casseroles.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep boiled potato in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑sized bags.
